attributes.scope: MWCC GC 1.2.5 family; applies to functions above the project's ~4000-insn fuzzy-arbitration threshold when a batch of several de-fakematch field conversions is applied and gated in one shot.

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: objdiff's fuzzy_match_percent, the mandated arbitration metric for functions over ~4000 instructions, is a coarser similarity measure than fndiff's real (raw diff-line) count and can move in the OPPOSITE direction from a genuine structural regression hidden inside a multi-field batch. Verified in PlayerMotion (4775 insns): a batch converting field_128(0x128) together with 3 known-safe fields (stat_damage/light_range/vibe_on/level) scored fuzzy 97.188065% - fractionally ABOVE the true-safe checkpoint's 97.18346% - while fndiff --count showed real jumped 3782->3963 and insn count went from an exact 4775/4775 match to an off-by-one 4775/4774; isolating field_128 alone reproduced the real regression standalone (3782->3963) with the other 3 fields confirmed neutral. Consequence: even when arbitrating a large function by fuzzy per project policy, ALSO check fndiff --count's insn-count-parity and real-line-count on every batch before accepting it - a fuzzy non-regression is not sufficient proof of no regression when several fields are converted together; bisect to single-field granularity (or small groups) whenever real disagrees with fuzzy's direction, and keep only the sub-changes that hold real steady or improve it alongside fuzzy.
